findings.title: Boundary-uniform two-spine moment bound fails in core survival derivation
operative_hypotheses: All x in[0,L] and positive constants independent of macroscopic interval in Lemma15
findings.evidence: For any fixed d>0, xN=L-d is an admissible interior starting point. Exact tail plus lambda gap gives HL(xN)/N -> Kd=2e^beta e^(-mu*d)sinh(beta*d)/(ctilde I)>0. Lemma15 interval-independent C1 yields probability lower bound ->C1Kd/t>1 for a fixed t<C1Kd. Independently, the unique two-spine forward branching time is uniform[0,T], so Q^{2,T}[rh]=T^-1 integral_0^T E_x^Q[r(zeta_s)h(s,zeta_s)]ds. Spine drift=-betaL coth(betaL(L-y)) is uniformly bounded on[L-2d,L-d/2]. A fixed-time Brownian tube event has N-independent positive probability and HL>=cN on that interval, r=1/2,h(s)>=HL. Therefore Q_{xN}^{2,L^2}[rh]>=c' N/L^2 ->infinity, contradicting the exact bound after(94). ForT=tN, same term>=c'/t.
findings.admissibility: W=200(1-x)^2 on[0,1], zero otherwise, is C1 nonnegative. Rayleigh test sin(2pi*x) supported[0,1/2] gives lambda_infinity>=25-2pi^2>1/16; argument holds for any fully pushed admissibleW.
findings.core_dependency: False uniform bound controls Bonferroni pair term(94), gives(96)/Cor8, used byLemma17 survival ODE and Theorem1, which normalizes conditional genealogy limits.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Starting points are a fixed positive distance from the absorbing endpoint.
No cancellation can remove the positive initial expectation integral.
Long-time mixing does not remove contribution from[0,s0].
Lemma13 allows t^-(k-1); substituting t=L^2/N does not imply a uniform constant.
C1(T1) avoids Lemma15 contradiction but changes quantifiers and does not alone establish small-time limit(81).
Theorem1 is for fixed x; moving xN does not disprove that final theorem.
Cor8 itself is not declared false merely because its proof contains the false bound.
findings.repair: Retain spatial initial-layer term, restrict intermediate uniformity, or prove a weighted tail argument. Full replacement core derivation not supplied.
findings.impact: Demonstrated invalid core derivation, Major without a whole-paper failure claim.

findings.title: High-frequency positive-minimum proof is false, norm estimate locally repaired
locators: Lemma8(55) and following compactness argument, pp1410–1411 (physical29–30)
operative_hypotheses: W bounded C1 nonnegative support[0,1], Hp
findings.evidence: Setz_a(t)=a u_-a(t/a). It solves z''=-(2/a+W(t/a)/a^2)z,z0=0,z'0=1, so z_a->t uniformly. Thusa^2g2(-1/a)->1/3; g2 tends0 and has no positive minimum. The lower integral(55) has ordera^-3, not a^-1. ForW200(1-x)^2 independently computed a^2g2 values approach1/3.
findings.repair: Forlambda=-s^2/2, Volterra formula u=sin(sx)/s-(1/s)integral sin(s(x-y))W(y)u(y)dy. Gronwall supu<=e^(M/s)/s,error<=M e^(M/s)/s^2. Forlarges, L2sin/s>=1/(2s),error<=1/(4s); ||u||2^2>=1/(16s^2)=1/(32|lambda|). Remaining compactparameter range has positive integral by initialderivative1 andODEcontinuity. Full[0,L]norm>= [0,1]norm.

AdmissibleW numerical check is corroboration; asymptoticproof independent of floatingpoint precision.

independent_acceptance_check.scope: One focused independent check of existing findings; not a new full-paper review.

problem_checks.decisive_check: The actual journal model is dyadic unit-variance BBM with W nonnegative C1 supported[0,1], Hfp and L=logN/(mu-beta). From the exact hyperbolic tail and endpoint derivative gap, H_L(L-d)/N tends to K_d>0. The explicit interval-independent C1 in Lemma15 then makes its probability lower bound exceed1 for any fixed t<C1 K_d and largeN. Independently, unaccelerated Q^{2,L^2} after(94) has its one forward branch time uniform[0,L^2]; its expectation is L^-2 integral E[r h]ds. On[L-2d,L-d/2], the drift -beta_L coth(beta_L(L-y)) is uniformly bounded and H>=cN. A Brownian tube for fixed s0 has probability p>0 independently of N, so the expectation>=pcs0 N/(2L^2) diverges.
problem_checks.admissibility_check: W=200(1-x)^2 on[0,1] and0 afterwards is C1 on the half-line; on[0,1/2], W/2>=25 and the test sin(2pi x) has kinetic quotient2pi^2. Hence lambda_infinity>=25-2pi^2>1/16. The counterargument in fact applies to every admissible fully pushed potential.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Pages43-47 explicitly connect the false all-x bound to Bonferroni(94),(96), Cor8, Lemma17 and Theorem1. The unbarred Q and h(|v|,zeta) in(94) rule out an accelerated-time reinterpretation. Lemma13 gives t^-1, not a constant at t=L^2/N. Positive early contributions survive mixing. This establishes a core derivation error; it does not refute fixed-x Theorem1, declare Cor8 false solely from the proof, or claim a completed repair.

problem_checks.decisive_check: Section4 explicitly permits Hp without Hfp for4.1-4.2. The variational supremum for W_a=a(1-x)^2 is nonnegative,1/2-Lipschitz in a,0 at a0 and unbounded, so an admissible lambda_infinity1/32 exists. Then beta1/4,mu sqrt17/4,1<alpha<2 and w_L N~C N^(2-alpha)->infinity. The exact h(N)/H=e^(w_L N) outgrows1+O(N^(2-alpha)). Cor2 permits bounded continuous f on the nonnegative orthant: chi(x)e^-z yields0 on its compact support versus the strictly positive claimed limiting integral.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Time-independent Pi convergence survives. Main theorems explicitly assume Hfp, where w_L N->0. Thus an added range restriction repairs this auxiliary extension; it is not a main-regime counterexample.

problem_checks.decisive_check: The declared particle kernel is a Lebesgue density with diffusion1/2. Removing e^(mu(x-y)) gives (lambda-.5dyy-.5W)R=delta, requiring derivative jump-2. The printed product/omega with omega=psi phi-prime-psi-prime phi has jump-1. Independently F=psi v-prime-psi-prime v satisfies F-prime=2(lambda1-lambda)psi v, F(L)=0 and F(0)=omega by the exact normalization, yielding omega=2(xi+w_L)integral psi v. Hence the leading constant is2xi I, not xi I. For xi1/N and2<alpha<3, w_L/xi exceeds xi L, so its removal cannot have the printed relative error.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: Scaling fundamental solutions cannot change the jump; speed-measure conventions conflict with the stated density. Under Hfp the corrected inverse Wronskian still has orderN used in Lemmas11-12; no changed final variance or failure of those order estimates follows. Unread handbook page19 remains unread; W0 is only algebraic calibration.

problem_checks.decisive_check: With lambda=-a and z_a(t)=a u_-a(t/a), the exact ODE is z-double-prime=-(2/a+W(t/a)/a^2)z, z0=0,z-prime0=1. Its coefficient tends uniformly0, so z_a->t and a^2 g2(-1/a)->1/3. The claimed positive minimum is therefore false and the short integral is ordera^-3. The retained high-precision values corroborate this analytic limit and were reused with their original origin.
problem_checks.independent_repair_check: For lambda=-s^2/2, the Volterra sine formula gives sup|u|<=e^(M/s)/s and error<=M e^(M/s)/s^2. The free sine L2 norm is>=1/(2s) and error<=1/(4s) for large s, so ||u||2^2>=1/(16s^2)=1/(32|lambda|). On the remaining compact parameter range continuity and u-prime0=1 give a strictly positive minimum.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_scope: The original compactness argument is invalid but the claimed norm order is established by the local replacement, sufficient for the specified eigenfunction dependency. No new numerical run or interval certificate claimed.
